A congruence subgroup property for symmetric mapping class groups

Download PDF

  * Marco Boggi  ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0003-4527-3152^{1} 

## Abstract

We prove the congruence subgroup property for the centralizer of a finite subgroup G in the mapping class group of a hyperbolic oriented and connected surface of finite topological type S such that the genus of the quotient surface S/G is at most 2. As an application, we show that torsion elements in the mapping class group of a surface of genus \(\le 2\) are conjugacy distinguished.

## 1 Introduction

### 1.1 The congruence subgroup property

Let S be an oriented connected surface of negative Euler characteristic and finite type and let G be a finite group acting faithfully on S. The group G then identifies with a finite subgroup of the mapping class group \({\Gamma }(S)\) of the surface S and let us denote by \({\Gamma }(S)^G\) the centralizer of G in \({\Gamma }(S)\). Let \(\Pi \) be the fundamental group of S for some choice of base point. There is a natural faithful representation \(\rho _S: {\Gamma }(S)\hookrightarrow \operatorname {Out}(\Pi )\) which restricts to a faithful representation \(\rho _{S,G}: {\Gamma }(S)^G\hookrightarrow \operatorname {Out}(\Pi )\).

For an abstract group L, let us denote by \(\widehat{L}\) its profinite completion. The homomorphisms \(\rho _S\) and \(\rho _{S,G}\) then induce the homomorphisms of profinite groups:

$$\begin{aligned} \hat{\rho }_S: {{\widehat{\Gamma }}}(S)\rightarrow \operatorname {Out}({{\widehat{\Pi }}})\hspace{1cm}\text{ and }\hspace{1cm}\hat{\rho }_{S,G}: {{\widehat{\Gamma }}}(S)^G\rightarrow \operatorname {Out}({{\widehat{\Pi }}}). \end{aligned}$$

(1)

The congruence subgroup problem for the mapping class group \({\Gamma }(S)\) (resp. for \({\Gamma }(S)^G\) ) asks whether the homomorphism \(\hat{\rho }_S\) (resp. \(\hat{\rho }_{S,G}\)) is faithful.

More conventionally, this question can be reformulated by asking whether, for every finite index subgroup \({\Gamma }\) of \({\Gamma }(S)\) (resp. of \({\Gamma }(S)^G\)), there exists a finite index characteristic subgroup K of \(\Pi \) such that the kernel of the induced representation \({\Gamma }(S)\rightarrow \operatorname {Out}(\Pi /K)\) (resp. \({\Gamma }(S)^G\rightarrow \operatorname {Out}(\Pi /K)\)) is contained in \({\Gamma }\).

The congruence subgroup problem for \({\Gamma }(S)\) was originally posed by Ivanov [7] and is known to have a positive answer for \(g(S)\le 2\), where g(S) denotes the genus of S. More precisely, the genus 0 case is discussed in [1, 9], the genus 1 case is treated in [1], and the genus 2 case in [2, 5].

Let \(S_{/G}:=S/G\) be the quotient of the surface S for the action of G and let \(p_G: S\rightarrow S_{/G}\) be the quotient map. Let R and B be, respectively, the ramification and the branch locus of \(p_G\) and put \(S^\circ :=S\smallsetminus R\) and \(S_{/G}^\circ :=S_{/G}\smallsetminus B\). The main result of the paper is then (cf. Theorem 4.1 for a slightly more general result):

### Theorem A

Let S be an oriented connected hyperbolic surface of finite type and G a finite group acting faithfully on S. If the congruence subgroup property holds for the mapping class group \({\Gamma }(S_{/G}^\circ )\) of the surface \(S_{/G}^\circ \), then it holds for the centralizer \({\Gamma }(S)^G\) of G in the mapping class group \({\Gamma }(S)\) of S.

In particular, we have:

### Corollary B

If \(g(S_{/G})\le 2\), then the congruence subgroup property holds for \({\Gamma }(S)^G\).

By Corollary 2.5, Brun\(_n(M)\) is a normal subgroup of \(B_n(M)\) for \(n \ge 3\). As an abstract group, Brun\(_n(M)\) is a free group of infinite rank for \(n \ge 3\) with \(M \ne S^2\) or \(\mathbb{RP}^2\), for \(n \ge 5\) with \(M = S^2\) and for \(n \ge 4\) with \(M = \mathbb{RP}^2\). A natural question is whether the factor group \(B_n(M)/\mathrm{Brun}_n(M)\) is finitely presented. Our answer to this question is positive.

**Theorem 1.2**  *Let \(M\) be a connected compact 2-manifold. Then the factor groups \(P_n(M)/\mathrm{Brun}_n(M)\) and \(B_n(M)/\mathrm{Brun}_n(M)\) are finitely presented for each \(n \ge 3\).*

The article is organized as follows. In Section 2, we give a review on Brunnian braids. The determination of a generating set for Brunnian braids is given in Section 3.
